items.fullText: 경제 한경 PREMIUM9 AI를 넘어서는 성공투자 구독하기 AI 추천 뉴스 AI 추천 뉴스 팝업 닫기 500kW 이하는 '전용 시장' 신설…소규모 태양광 사업자들 주목 입력 2026.10.01 13:07 수정 2026.10.01 13:07 기사 스크랩 기사 스크랩 댓글 댓글 기사 공유 공유 글자크기 조절 글자크기 프린트 프린트 김리안 기자 구독하기 구글 검색 선호 출처로 추가 Google 검색에서 한국경제 기사를 더 자주 볼 수 있습니다. 사진=연합뉴스 정부가 15년간 운영해온 재생에너지 공급의무화제도(RPS)를 경쟁입찰 기반 장기계약시장으로 전환하는 하위법령 개편안을 내놓은 가운데, 일부 시민단체에서 “대기업·공기업에만 물량을 몰아줘 에너지민주주의를 훼손한다”는 반발이 나왔다. 이에 대해 정부는 “소규모 및 주민참여형 태양광 시장을 오히려 확대·보호하는 장치가 마련돼 있다”며 즉각 진화에 나섰다. 실제로 정부 개편안에는 500kW 이하 소규모 전용 시장을 별도로 개설하고 주민참여형 사업에 정책적 우대가격을 보장하는 안전장치가 담겨 있다. 1일 업계 등에 따르면 태양광 관련 시민단체들은 전날 서울 강남구 엘리에나호텔에서 열린 공청회장 앞에서 기자회견을 열고 “정부의 RPS 개편안은 2030년 태양광 목표 중 대부분을 발전공기업과 대형 민간 발전사 등에 몰아주고 직접 건설이나 지분투자 실적만 인정하겠다는 계획”이라며 “거대 자본 중심의 구조로 시민 참여와 에너지민주주의를 질식시키는 개악”이라고 주장했다. 그러나 이는 사실과 다르다는 게 정부 입장이다. 정부는 설비용량 500kW 이하 소규모 설비가 대기업과 맞붙지 않도록 ‘별도 계약시장’을 운영하고, 햇빛소득마을 등 주민참여형 사업과 영농·건물형 태양광에는 정책적 우대가격을 유지해 소규모·시민참여 시장을 계속 키우고 보급을 넓혀갈 계획이라는 설명이다. 소규모 사업자들이 1MW 이상 가상발전소(VPP) 형태로 묶여 참여할 경우 추가 인센티브를 부여하고, 재생에너지 종합서비스기업(RESCO)을 통해 입찰과 사후관리까지 전주기 밀착 지원한다는 방침도 개편안에 명시했다. 정부가 추진하는 RPS 개편의 핵심은 2012년부터 15년간 이어진 가격 변동성 문제를 바로잡고 시장 경쟁을 통해 발전단가를 안정화하는 데 있다. 기존 체제에서는 재생에너지 사업자가 재생에너지공급인증서(REC) 가격 출렁임에 노출돼 안정적인 수익을 예측하기 어려웠고, 매년 급증하는 RPS 정산비용이 전기요금 인상 압박으로 작용했다. 전력거래소의 RPS 현물시장 가격이 일반 기업의 RE100(재생에너지 100%) 조달 단가까지 끌어올리는 악순환도 발생했다. 새 제도에 따라 내년부터 신규 진입하는 태양광·풍력 발전소는 정부가 제시한 가격 아래에서 경쟁입찰을 치른다. 낙찰자는 한전과 장기간 고정가격 계약을 체결해 전력시장가격과의 차액을 정산받는다. 입찰 평가에는 가격 외에도 주민수용성, 국내 공급망 기여도, 계통 영향 등 비가격 지표가 종합 반영된다. 기존 사업자의 충격을 최소화하기 위해 기존 설비의 REC 발급은 원칙적으로 최대 20년간 인정되고 현물시장도 2029년 말까지 3년간 유예 운영되지만, 신규 사업자는 입찰시장 진입으로 단일화된다. 정부는 공청회와 입법예고, 관계부처 협의를 거쳐 연말까지 시행령·시행규칙 개정을 마무리하고, 내년 초 고시 제정과 함께 제1차 계약시장 입찰을 공고할 계획이다. 기후부 관계자는 “앞으로도 이해관계자들과 충분히 소통하며 세부 제도를 정교하게 설계해나갈 것”이라고 말했다. 김리안 기자 knra@hankyung.com 좋아요 싫어요 후속기사 원해요 ⓒ 한경닷컴, 무단전재 및 재배포 금지 한국경제 구독신청 한경 프리미엄9 구독신청 김리안 기자 한국경제 김리안 기자입니다. 기후위기 시대에 에너지·자원 이슈를 산업과 투자적 관점에서 전해드립니다. 프리미엄9을 구독하시면 더 Deep

items.t: DoorDash’s drone strategy started on the ground
items.d: DoorDash unveiled the six-propeller aircraft that will be used in its new drone delivery business at its annual Dash Forward 2026 event.
items.fullText: When DoorDash set out to build a drone delivery business , it started with the tricky logistics that happen on the ground before it looked up. The autonomous drone came last, according to the company, which unveiled its new six-propeller aircraft at its annual Dash Forward 2026 event on Wednesday. Before DoorDash worked on the aircraft, the company focused on ground infrastructure, including loading systems, how food would be handed off from a restaurant’s kitchen, and packaging. DoorDash Labs, the R&D team that built its autonomous sidewalk delivery bot Dot, created the drone delivery service now called DoorDash Air. The same team also developed the underlying software, called the Autonomous Delivery Platform (ADP), to handle the coordination challenges in deliveries handled by humans, sidewalk delivery bots, and now drones. The ADP software uses smart routing, incorporating factors like weather, flight range, and ground traffic to narrow down which orders actually make sense to send by air. Image Credits: DoorDash The company’s systems-first strategy for its DoorDash Air business aligns with its strengths. DoorDash isn’t a hardware company, but it is sitting on 13 years of user data from the merchant and customer sides of the business. (DoorDash has previously disclosed that more than 500,000 restaurants are on its delivery marketplace.) The company says it sized the whole DoorDash Air system around its historical order data, including how much orders weigh and how far they typically travel. “We didn’t start with a drone and ask what would fit,” Harrison Shih, who heads up DoorDash Air, said in a statement. “We started with what people order and how local businesses actually operate, then built the entire system from there.” DoorDash announced plans in July to launch the drone delivery business after receiving a Part 135 air carrier certification from the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration. items.t: Reddit is killing RSS feeds and ending public API access because of AI bots
items.d: Reddit is ending support for RSS feeds, as the company continues tightening access to its trove of user-generated content.
items.fullText: Amid a number of updates for moderators and developers announced Wednesday, comes bad news for supporters of a more open web: Reddit is ending support for RSS feeds. Reddit says RSS has now become a “common surface for large-scale scraping and automated abuse,” which is why it’s made the decision to wind down RSS feeds on its platform. “We know RSS has been a beloved part of the open web for a long time, and we’re grateful to everyone who used it to stay connected to Reddit,” the company noted in its announcement, where it also shared a March 2027 shutdown date for its public API. Reddit said RSS support will cease on November 13. RSS, or Really Simple Syndication/Rich Site Summary, is a web feed that lets users and applications access updates to a website in a standardized format. The format became particularly popular in the blogging era, as it offered a way to subscribe to a site’s new posts in a news-reading app. Google once operated the most popular of these, but shut it down in 2013 , ceding the market to companies like Feedly and other indie applications. The decision to kill Reddit’s RSS feeds comes at a time when the site’s treasure trove of user-generated content in its forums has become a profitable side business for the company in the form of AI licensing deals. During its second quarter , Reddit said its “other revenue” beyond advertising had grown 24% year-over-year to $43 million. It’s no wonder that Reddit doesn’t want to give any of that data away for free. For moderators who have relied on RSS channels for their own alerts, Reddit is now recommending a shift to the Discord Relay Devvit app. The company suggested that moderators and their teams review their setups and migrate their workflows before the shutdown date of November 13 to ensure there’s no disruption. items.t: Senate Democrats block Husted-led bill on data centers, calling it ‘toothless’
items.d: The bill aims to prevent data centers from spiking local utility costs. Republicans accused Democrats of playing political games, noting the bill passed the House 417-3.
items.fullText: Artificial intelligence Senate Democrats block Husted-led bill on data centers, calling it ‘toothless’ The bill aims to prevent data centers from spiking local utility costs. Republicans accused Democrats of playing political games, noting the bill passed the House 417-3. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 Sen. Jon Husted, R-Ohio. Kevin Dietsch / Getty Images file Share Add NBC News to Google Sept. 30, 2026, 1:41 PM EDT By Sahil Kapur WASHINGTON — Senate Democrats blocked legislation Wednesday aimed at protecting consumers from paying higher prices when new data centers are built in their communities. The vote was 57-43, short of the 60 needed to break a filibuster. The Ratepayer Protection Act , which passed the House by a vote of 417-3 two weeks ago, would set a federal standard on the issue. It would also instruct state public utility commissions to find ways to make developers of data centers that use huge amounts of energy cover their own costs of water and electricity to consumers. The Senate version is led by appointed Sen. Jon Husted, R-Ohio, who’s locked in a competitive battle as he seeks his first full Senate term. He is facing heat at home from Democratic rival Sherrod Brown, a former senator who has branded him “the face of data centers” for promoting developments when he was lieutenant governor. “I heard they said they wanted lower electricity prices,” Husted said of Democrats on Tuesday. “All they have to do is not block it, vote for it, and it will be on the president’s desk, and we will have a bipartisan win.” Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., said the bill would be merely “optional” for states and wouldn’t achieve much beyond partisan messaging for Republicans. “Plain and simple, the Ratepayer Protection Act is a fraud,” Schumer told reporters Tuesday. “It does not require any protections at all. While Americans are demanding real guardrails on AI and data centers, Republicans are offering a toothless messaging bill.

items.t: Meta disputes claim that Muse read a user’s private messages without permission
items.d: Meta says its Muse AI agent cannot access a user’s Messages without explicit permission, disputing a journalist’s account that the agent read his private messages while the required Mac setting was turned off.
items.fullText: Meta is fighting back against a journalist’s claim that its AI agent Muse read the user’s private messages without permission. Following an earlier report from Inc. columnist Jason Aten that detailed the issue, Meta VP of Communications Andy Stone pushed back , making it clear that the company does not believe its product did this without the user’s consent. “The Messages integration in the Muse app for Mac is entirely opt-in,” Stone wrote on X in response to the claims made by the piece. “You have to enable both Full Disk Access and the Messages connector for Muse to be able to read your Messages content. It can’t read your Messages unless you do this.” Despite Meta’s denial, many people are still suspicious that Meta isn’t being truthful. That’s not surprising , given the tech giant’s years of mishandling consumer data , which has led to lawsuits , FTC violations , and fines . Just days ago, for instance, a New Mexico jury determined the tech giant had misled users about its data practices in a case that resulted from the 2018 Cambridge Analytica data breach scandal. Whether users can trust Muse will be a deciding factor in whether or not Meta wins the consumer AI market. Although its app is faring well now, and remains No. 1 on the App Store, Meta’s reputation may not recover if more reports like this emerge, true or not. If anything, the company should be engaging with the journalist directly to determine how this could have possibly happened, instead of just denying that it did. items.fullText: AI Security Is an Engineering Problem — How to Solve It at Every Layer of the Agent Stack Open research, controls across the agent stack and continuous testing help defenders build and operate more secure AI systems. September 21, 2026 by Saša Zdjelar 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! AI security is an engineering problem. That means defined security requirements, enforceable controls, named owners and evidence that protections work. As AI becomes more capable, the industry must accelerate security engineering, broaden access to defensive tools and share what works faster. Technology Changes, Security Fundamentals Endure The internet and cloud computing changed how software operates, while core security responsibilities endured: establish identity, control access, limit exposure and verify that protections work. AI agents introduce new capabilities — reasoning , using tools and adapting actions based on the data they encounter. Those capabilities require applying established principles to new operating conditions. This pace creates pressure. Organizations want the productivity benefits of AI while the practices to govern and secure these systems are still developing. Security Depends on the Full Agent Stack Applications depend on code, data, identities, services and infrastructure. Security depends on how those components work together — and AI agents extend that system . Models provide capabilities; harnesses organize context, tools and workflows; and runtime environments provide the infrastructure within which actions execute. Each part of that stack carries security responsibilities, and proper protection requires controls across each layer, as data, instructions and actions move through the system. Air pollution is a serious public health risk, contributing to an estimated 30,000 deaths in the U.K. alone last year. Data-driven insights can help — but computing air quality with traditional chemistry-based models is expensive, which limits how detailed they can be and how regularly they can be run. David Topping, a professor in the University of Manchester’s department of Earth and environmental science, saw that the NVIDIA Earth-2 family of open AI models and tools had cracked a related problem for weather forecasting — and asked whether the same generative frameworks could work for pollution fields. “The biggest challenge is the compute required to forecast air quality,” said Topping. “Once you put chemistry into weather models, they get really, really slow. So I said, why don’t we try using the generative frameworks that NVIDIA develops for climate and weather for pollution fields?” Working with the NVIDIA Earth-2 team, Topping and colleagues generated training data from existing chemistry-climate simulations, then trained Earth-2 CorrDiff — a generative downscaling model — on Isambard-AI, the U.K.’s national AI supercomputer in Bristol. The model worked on the first attempt. The team has since added Earth-2 StormCast, a model that enables time-dependent forecasts that directly use air quality observations, and showed the test-training and inference workflows running on the NVIDIA DGX Spark personal AI supercomputer. “To improve human health, it’s essential that we understand the impact of environmental stressors in the air we breathe,” said Topping. “Our U.K.-wide pollution model allows u

items.fullText: ‘Now We Can Know Everything and Do Anything,’ Jensen Huang Says at Dreamforce At Dreamforce, Salesforce and NVIDIA announced Koa, a CRM reasoning model for Agentforce, post-trained from Nemotron on 27 years of Salesforce CRM intelligence — and running entirely within Salesforce’s own infrastructure. September 15, 2026 by Brian Caulfield 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Know everything. Do anything. That was the message NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang brought to Salesforce Dreamforce Tuesday, joining CEO Marc Benioff onstage in an appearance that coincided with the announcement of Koa — Salesforce’s first CRM reasoning model, built on NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Super. Huang didn’t just take the stage. He walked into the crowd — threading through the audience at Moscone Center, mic in hand, with Benioff alongside. “We’re all following you, bro,” Benioff told Huang at one point, drawing applause. “With electricity, we could power everything,” Huang said, tracing the arc of industrial revolutions. “With the internet, you can find anything. And now, with artificial intelligence as an infrastructure layer across the planet, we can know everything and do anything.” That arc led directly to the announcement. Salesforce’s first reasoning model was built by post-training NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Super on a proprietary synthetic dataset drawn from nearly three decades of enterprise CRM deployments. AI Safety When Benioff asked Huang about AI safety, Huang was direct. “Safety is paramount in a lot of ways. It’s job one,” Huang said. “However, safety is an engineering problem.
